To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

role conflict and role conflict are empirically distinct constructs, and that role conflict and ambiguity are related to organizational and managerial variables, to member satisfaction, anxiety and intention to leave, and to each other in expected directions.

the role conflict and role conflict and role confusion constructs have been identified and operationalized in a way that permits the study of these phenomena in organizations, that these constructs have a high level of reliability, that they are empirically distinguishable, and that they are related in expected directions to other variables.
role conflict and ambiguity are distinct, and that they are related to a variety of organizational variables.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement of role conflict and the measurement of role ambiguity, and their relationships with other variables.

the measurement of role conflict and the development of a conceptual model of its relationship with organizational and managerial practices, leader behavior, member satisfaction, anxiety and propensity to leave.
the development and testing, of questionnaire measures of the role constructs of role conflict and ambiguous.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role conflict- ambiguity constructs have been demonstrated to have some degree of validity as measures of role phenomena in complex organizations.
the two measures of role construct are valid and reliable, and are useful in the study of complex organizations.
role conflict and role ambiguities are not only important in their own right but also that they have a pervasive impact on other variables in the organization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the measures of the role constructs are reliable and valid, and the constructs themselves are important to the study of organizations.
role conflict and ambiguity are important organizational phenomena, and that they are related to important organizational outcomes.
the measures of role conflict, ambiguity, and related constructs have been found to have satisfactory psychometric properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
role conflict and role conflict are two separate constructs that can be reliably assessed.
role conflict and ambiguity, as measured by the scales we have developed and validated, are independent of one another and have differential relations with organizational variables.
these two role constructs, while related, are not the same, and they are not simply measures of the same thing.
